overview: This Senate resolution supports September 2026 as "Sickle Cell Disease Awareness Month." Sickle cell disease is an inherited blood disorder that can cause severe pain, strokes, organ damage and shortened lives; the resolution says it affects about 100,000 Americans and occurs most often among Black Americans, though it is also found in other groups. It notes that many children with the disease do not get recommended stroke screening or preventive medicine, that the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved two gene therapies that can cure it, and that many states take part in a Medicare and Medicaid agency program to help Medicaid patients get those therapies. The resolution encourages Americans to hold events raising awareness of the disease, the sickle cell trait, and available care. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on September 30, 2026.
for: Supporters say awareness can encourage screening, testing for the sickle cell trait and use of new treatments by families who may not know about them.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic: it does not change any law or provide new funding for research or treatment.
